title_en: Li Guangping — case of transportation and illegal possession of narcotics
keywords_en: criminal; drug crime; first instance; grassroots people's court; Beijing; natural person; criminal law; distinction between drug trafficking and illegal possession of drugs; determination of attempted crime; application of old and new criminal law; partial support; drug delivery by mail; illegal possession of drugs; heroin; drugs
full_text_en:
Li Guangping — transport of and illegal possession of narcotics

Defendant: Li Guangping, male, 33 years old, native of Hangzhou City, Zhejiang Province, salesman of Hangzhou Xingguang Industry and Trade Company. Arrested on July 14, 1997.

The Beijing Haidian District People's Procuratorate initiated a public prosecution against the defendant Li Guangping for the crime of illegal possession of narcotics, and brought the case to the Beijing Haidian District People's Court. The Haidian District People's Court, after public trial, found the following facts:

At noon on June 12, 1997, the defendant Li Guangping, at the post office of the Beijing Post Office located in the New Century Hotel, sent 6 grams of heroin to Chen Yong in Hangzhou City, Zhejiang Province by international express mail, and was discovered and reported. In the afternoon of the same day, Li Guangping was apprehended by public security officers in Room 2112 of the New Century Hotel, where he was renting. The public security officers also immediately searched and seized 31.41 grams of heroin from Li Guangping's person. Li Guangping stated that the narcotics were purchased from Guangzhou. All narcotics have now been confiscated.

The above facts are confirmed by the testimony of witnesses Jin Siyu, Zhao Weitao, and Chen Yong, the Beijing Public Security Bureau's criminal science and technology inspection report, the narcotics confiscation list, physical evidence photographs, the Beijing Public Security Bureau's criminal science and technology identification report, and the certificate of arrest issued by the public security organ. The defendant Li Guangping also confessed to the facts.

The Beijing Haidian District People's Court held: The facts that the defendant Li Guangping mailed 6 grams of heroin and illegally possessed 31.41 grams of heroin are clear and the evidence is reliable. Mailing articles is a business conducted by the postal department to move the mailed articles from place A to place B according to the sender's request. The postal department uses means of transport to achieve the spatial displacement of the mailed articles from place A to place B. Therefore, in Article 2 of the "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the 'Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Prohibiting Narcotics'" issued by the Supreme People's Court on December 20, 1994, mailing narcotics is stipulated as a criminal method under the crime of transporting narcotics. The "Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China" was revised on March 14, 1997, and came into effect on October 1 of the same year. The acts charged against Li Guangping occurred before the implementation of the revised Criminal Law. Pursuant to Article 12 of the revised Criminal Law, criminal liability should be investigated according to the Criminal Law before revision. The revised Criminal Law shall apply only if it does not deem the act a crime or imposes a lighter punishment. Mailing or illegally possessing heroin is considered a criminal act under both the Criminal Law before and after revision. However, under the "Decision on Prohibiting Narcotics" before the revision of the Criminal Law, the punishment was heavier than under the revised Criminal Law. Now that the revised Criminal Law has been implemented, it should be applied to this case. Li Guangping's act of mailing heroin violates the provision of Article 347, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law that "whoever smuggles, traffics, transports, or manufactures narcotics, regardless of the quantity, shall be investigated for criminal liability and subjected to criminal punishment." His conduct has constituted the crime of transporting narcotics. Because his act of mailing narcotics was discovered in time and thus failed, it constitutes an attempted crime. Pursuant to Article 23 of the Criminal Law, he may be given a lighter punishment compared to a completed offender. Li Guangping, knowing it was heroin, refused to surrender it and illegally possessed it, and there is no evidence to prove whether the narcotics were for sale or for his own consumption. The quantity of narcotics he possessed meets the provisions of Article 348 of the Criminal Law, and his conduct has constituted the crime of illegal possession of narcotics. Li Guangping committed two crimes as one person, and should be sentenced to concurrent punishment for several crimes pursuant to Article 69 of the Criminal Law. Accordingly, on November 6, 1997, the Haidian District People's Court rendered the following judgment:

The defendant Li Guangping is convicted of the crime of transporting narcotics and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of one year and six months, and a fine of RMB 5,000; he is convicted of the crime of illegal possession of narcotics and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of two years and ten months, and a fine of RMB 20,000. The combined sentence is fixed-term imprisonment of three years and six months, and a fine of RMB 25,000 (to be paid within two years after release from prison).

After the first instance judgment was announced, the defendant Li Guangping did not appeal. The first instance judgment has become legally effective.
